title.sl: Kar ni tako: if I had, I'd
title.de: Was nicht so ist: if I had, I'd
title.it: Ciò che non è così: if I had, I'd
title.en: What isn't so: if I had, I'd

rule.sl:
Kar ni tako ali se skoraj gotovo ne bo zgodilo: **if** + preteklik, v drugem delu **would**: **If I had a boat, I'd row across.** (Če bi {m:imel|f:imela} čoln, bi {m:veslal|f:veslala} čez.) Čolna nimam. Preteklik tu ne pomeni prej, ampak *ni zares*. **'d** je **would**.

Drugi del ima lahko tudi **could** ali **might**: **If it stopped raining, we could go out.** Dela lahko zamenjata mesti, brez vejice: **I'd row across if I had a boat.** Vprašanje: **What would you do if you won the raffle?**

Pri be pisava želi **were** za vse osebe: **If I were you, I'd wait.** (nasvet: Na tvojem mestu bi {m:počakal|f:počakala}.) Ljudje rečejo tudi **was** (*If I was you*), v govoru je to prav.

Pisava ima would samo v drugem delu: **If I had a boat**. Slovenščina ima *bi* v obeh delih, marsikje pa ljudje rečejo tudi *If I would have a boat*.

Primerjaj: **If I have time, I'll help.** (Morda bom {m:imel|f:imela} čas.) **If I had time, I'd help.** (Časa nimam.)
rule.de:
Was nicht so ist oder kaum sein wird: **if** + Vergangenheit, im anderen Teil **would**: **If I had a boat, I'd row across.** (Wenn ich ein Boot hätte, würde ich hinüberrudern.) Ich habe keines. Die Vergangenheit heißt hier nicht *früher*, sondern *nicht wirklich*. **'d** ist **would**.

Der andere Teil kann auch **could** oder **might** haben: **If it stopped raining, we could go out.** Die Teile können tauschen, dann ohne Komma: **I'd row across if I had a boat.** Frage: **What would you do if you won the raffle?**

Bei be will die Schrift **were** für alle Personen: **If I were you, I'd wait.** (Rat: An deiner Stelle würde ich warten.) Man sagt auch **was** (*If I was you*), gesprochen ist das richtig.

Die Schrift hat would nur im anderen Teil: **If I had a boat**. Deutsch kann *wenn ich haben würde* sagen, und manche Leute sagen auch *If I would have a boat*.

Vergleiche: **If I have time, I'll help.** (Vielleicht habe ich Zeit.) **If I had time, I'd help.** (Ich habe keine.)
rule.it:
Ciò che non è così o quasi certamente non sarà: **if** + il passato, **would** nell'altra parte: **If I had a boat, I'd row across.** (Se avessi una barca, remerei fino all'altra riva.) Non ce l'ho. Il passato qui non vuol dire *prima*, ma *non davvero*. **'d** è **would**.

L'altra parte può avere anche **could** o **might**: **If it stopped raining, we could go out.** Le parti possono scambiarsi, allora senza virgola: **I'd row across if I had a boat.** Per chiedere: **What would you do if you won the raffle?**

Con be lo scritto vuole **were** per tutte le persone: **If I were you, I'd wait.** (Un consiglio: Se fossi in te, aspetterei.) Si dice anche **was** (*If I was you*), a voce è giusto.

Lo scritto ha would solo nell'altra parte: **If I had a boat**. Dopo se l'italiano usa il congiuntivo, e in certi posti si sente anche *If I would have a boat*.

Confronta: **If I have time, I'll help.** (Forse avrò tempo.) **If I had time, I'd help.** (Non ne ho.)
rule.en:
What isn't so, or probably won't be: **if** + the past, **would** in the other half: **If I had a boat, I'd row across.** (I haven't got one.) The past here doesn't mean earlier: it means *not really*. **'d** is **would**.

The other half can also have **could** or **might**: **If it stopped raining, we could go out.** The halves can change places, then with no comma: **I'd row across if I had a boat.** To ask: **What would you do if you won the raffle?**

With be, writing wants **were** for every person: **If I were you, I'd wait.** (advice) People also say **was** (*If I was you*), and in talk that's right.

Writing has would only in the other half: **If I had a boat**. In some places people also say *If I would have a boat*.

Compare: **If I have time, I'll help.** (I may have.) **If I had time, I'd help.** (I haven't.)

rule.sl: Kar ni tako: **if** + preteklik, potem **would**: **If I had a boat, I'd row across.** Tudi **could**, **might**. Pri be **were**, govorjeno tudi **was**: **If I were you, I'd wait.** Kar se lahko zgodi: **If I have time, I'll help.**
rule.de: Was nicht so ist: **if** + Vergangenheit, dann **would**: **If I had a boat, I'd row across.** Auch **could**, **might**. Bei be **were**, gesprochen auch **was**: **If I were you, I'd wait.** Was passieren kann: **If I have time, I'll help.**
rule.it: Ciò che non è così: **if** + il passato, poi **would**: **If I had a boat, I'd row across.** Anche **could**, **might**. Con be **were**, a voce anche **was**: **If I were you, I'd wait.** Ciò che può succedere: **If I have time, I'll help.**
rule.en: What isn't so: **if** + the past, then **would**: **If I had a boat, I'd row across.** Also **could**, **might**. With be **were**, spoken also **was**: **If I were you, I'd wait.** What may happen: **If I have time, I'll help.**

examples.en: If Mr Tyson sold the mill, he'd move to Keswick.
examples.sl: Če bi gospod Tyson prodal mlin, bi se preselil v Keswick.
examples.de: Wenn Mr Tyson die Mühle verkaufte, würde er nach Keswick ziehen.
examples.it: Se Mr Tyson vendesse il mulino, si trasferirebbe a Keswick.

examples.en: If I were you, I'd take a coat.
examples.de: An deiner Stelle würde ich einen Mantel mitnehmen.
examples.it: Se fossi in te, prenderei un cappotto.

tip.sl: 💡 Slovenščina ima *bi* v obeh delih, pisana angleščina would samo v enem: **If I had**, potem **I'd**.
tip.de: 💡 Deutsch kann *wenn ich haben würde* sagen, die Schrift im Englischen nur **If I had**, dann **I'd**.
tip.it: 💡 L'italiano dopo se ha il congiuntivo, l'inglese il semplice passato: **If I had**, poi **I'd**.
tip.en: 💡 **If I had**, then **I'd**: writing keeps would to the other half.
